note: The public ledger of content Orrery could not source under its licensing bar (Creative Commons / public domain, no watermark, authentic — no fan reproductions). We would rather show an honest gap than ship something we don't have the right to use. Append new walls here as we hit them.

gaps.want: Authentic program and mission patches for the early Soviet crewed programs, to sit beside the NASA insignia.
gaps.wall: Two walls at once. First, most never existed: the USSR did not adopt the mission-patch tradition until Apollo–Soyuz in 1975, so Vostok, Voskhod and the first Soyuz flights simply had no patch. Second, what does exist later — Soyuz TM/TMA expedition patches, Roscosmos emblems — is copyrighted or uploaded only under fair-use, never released under a free licence.

Modern fan reproductions (e.g. a CC-BY Buran emblem by a game artist) — freely licensed but not authentic insignia
gaps.resolution: The Roscosmos agency logo stands in as the honest mark on every affected program card and page.

gaps.want: The China Manned Space (CMS) programme emblem and Shenzhou crew patches, to sit beside the NASA insignia on the Tiangong and Shenzhou pages.
gaps.wall: China's crewed programme does use mission patches — every Shenzhou crew has one — but the CMS emblem and the Shenzhou insignia are held under copyright by the China Manned Space Agency, not released under a free licence. Wikimedia Commons carries none of them; the only free-licensed images returned for these searches are unrelated NASA photographs.

Wikimedia Commons — China Manned Space Agency logo
rejected: cmse.gov.cn and Chinese state media imagery — copyrighted, no free licence
Third-party fan reproductions of Shenzhou patches — not authentic and not free
gaps.resolution: The CNSA agency logo stands in as the honest mark on the Tiangong and Shenzhou cards and pages.

gaps.want: Programme and mission insignia for Japan's JAXA and India's ISRO, to sit beside the NASA patches on their programme pages.
gaps.wall: Both agencies do produce mission logos and emblems — Hayabusa2, SLIM, Chandrayaan-3 and the rest all have them — but they are held under the agencies' own copyright and are not released under a free licence. Wikimedia Commons carries none of them; the only free-licensed results for these searches are unrelated NASA photographs.

gaps.resolution: The JAXA and ISRO agency logos stand in as the honest mark on the affected programme cards and pages.
